statement: Cejel's v27 A1 pytest-settings reader (#626) returned nothing for a run it could not read whole: a path argument holding a variable, an expression as its working directory, -c outside the repository, --pyargs, Jenkins dir(). The run then dropped out of the list, so the files it collects were read under pytest's defaults, and a setting that run really passes (tox -- -p no:skipping, nox posargs, an undefined make variable) never withheld the rule: the certificate said a file pytest runs "runs no test". Dropping an input you cannot read is an assertion that it holds nothing. Rules: a reader that cannot read part of its subject must model that part as unknown, with every effect the unknown could have, and name it in the output with the reason; it must never leave the part out. Before calling a reader done, list every place it returns early on input it does not understand, and check what the caller then assumes.

In cejel #633's fix, `name.replace(/[ \t]*\($/, '')` was written for a ten-character string and failed the ReDoS guard (src/__tests__/regex-redos-guard.test.ts), which runs every regex literal in the scan path against adversarial input whatever string the code applies it to: a blank run before a missing `(` backtracks at each start, quadratically. The same pass had two loops that searched for a closing `}` or `)` with indexOf after each opener; with many openers and no closer, each search runs to the end of the text, which is quadratic too. Rules: trim with indexOf and trimEnd, not a regex with a leading `[ \t]*`; in a scan for an opener and its closer, stop at the first opener whose closer is missing, since no later opener has one either; and run the ReDoS guard and the scaling tests before the first full-suite run, not after it.
